---
title: The Tidewatch Cantos
author: Anon
language: en
---

## Canto I

The lamp goes out along the quay,
the gulls come down to feed;
the tide that took my love from me
returns for me indeed.

I counted every plank and stone,
I named them one by one;
the harbour keeps me here alone
until the watch is done.

A sail, a sail against the grey,
a shape I dare not name;
it neither turns nor bears away
but burns without a flame.

## Canto II

Now morning walks the shingle bare
and finds the nets undone;
the salt has silvered all my hair
beneath a colder sun.

They ask me why I will not sleep,
why still I pace the shore;
I tell them that the water's deep
has one thing more in store.

The bell that has no rope to ring,
the door that has no key,
the song the drowned men cannot sing —
they keep the watch with me.
